document_genres: technical deep dive with case studies

source_claims.statement: Six years of work starting 2019. Classic detection methods blocked by WAFs. Shifted to parser discrepancy detection. 0.CL initially seemed unexploitable; developed double-desync and early-response gadgets. Expect header explored after 2022 attempts yielded nothing.
Timeout-based and gadget detection fingerprinted. 0.CL often deadlocks. Some findings low bounty or out of scope. Reporting delays with CDNs.

research_questions.formulation: After traditional CL.TE detection is mitigated, which parser discrepancies (including 0.CL and Expect) remain exploitable, and what early-response or sequencing techniques make them practical?
research_questions.anchor: shift from classic methods to discrepancy detection and Expect
research_questions.uncertainty_reduced: whether 0.CL and Expect can be made reliable
research_questions.assumption_challenged: that 0.CL is unexploitable and that WAFs close the class

environment_model_updates: HTTP/1.1 length ambiguity persists across proxies
Early-response gadgets exist on some servers (IIS /con)
Expect header can split requests and create new desyncs

systematic_vs_exploratory.systematic: HTTP Request Smuggler probing of header discrepancies
systematic_vs_exploratory.exploratory: Expect header after earlier attempts failed; double-desync after deadlocks

negative_inconclusive: Some CDN findings: delayed or out of scope
unobserved_history: exact 2022 Expect experiments that yielded nothing
forbidden_inferences: Do not treat WAF blocks as closure of the desync class
0.CL deadlock is a prerequisite problem, not a falsified hypothesis
next_evidence_actions: Cross-reference with SRC-000026, SRC-000027, SRC-000029 for shared lineage
layer_b_candidate_principles: When classic detection is mitigated, probe for parser discrepancies and early-response gadgets rather than abandoning the class
Sequencing techniques (double-desync) can convert an apparently unexploitable primitive into a usable one
model_vs_harness: Identifying Expect and sequencing techniques is model reasoning; large-scale discrepancy probing and tool support are harness.
